# ---------------------------------------------------------
# EXPORT HELPERS FOR PPT
# ---------------------------------------------------------
function plot_wigner_export(final_state, title_str, filename)
    # Traces out the spin (subsystem 1) to leave the motional mode[cite: 3]
    rho_motional = ptrace(final_state, 1) 
    
    b_fock = FockBasis(50)
    rho_fock = DenseOperator(b_fock, rho_motional.data)

    x_vec = -4.0:0.1:4.0
    p_vec = -4.0:0.1:4.0
    W = wigner(rho_fock, x_vec, p_vec)

    fig = figure(figsize=(7, 5.5))
    subplots_adjust(bottom=0.15, left=0.15, top=0.9, right=0.95)

    PyPlot.pcolormesh(x_vec, p_vec, W, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-0.1, vmax=0.3, shading="nearest")
    cbar = PyPlot.colorbar()
    cbar.set_label("Wigner Function W(x, p)", labelpad=15)

    PyPlot.plot([0], [0], "w+", markersize=15, markeredgewidth=2, label="Original Vacuum |0>")
    
    PyPlot.xlabel("Position (x)", fontsize=12)
    PyPlot.ylabel("Momentum (p)", fontsize=12)
    PyPlot.title(title_str, fontsize=14, pad=15)
    PyPlot.grid(color="white", alpha=0.2)
    
    # Save the figure automatically for the PPT
    savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    display(fig)
end

function plot_spin_density(state, title_str, filename)
    # Trace out the motional mode (subsystem 2) to get the spin density matrix
    rho_spin = ptrace(state, 2)
    
    fig, ax = PyPlot.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    
    # Plot absolute values of the 2x2 density matrix
    Z = abs.(rho_spin.data)
    cax = ax.matshow(Z, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1)
    fig.colorbar(cax, label="Absolute Value |ρ|")
    
    # Add matrix values as text annotations
    for (i, j) in Iterators.product(1:2, 1:2)
        val = round(Z[i, j], digits=3)
        ax.text(j-1, i-1, string(val), ha="center", va="center", color="black", fontsize=14)
    end
    
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1])
    ax.set_xticklabels(["|g⟩", "|e⟩"], fontsize=14)
    ax.set_yticks([0, 1])
    ax.set_yticklabels(["⟨g|", "⟨e|"], fontsize=14)
    
    PyPlot.title(title_str, fontsize=14, pad=20)
    savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    display(fig)
end

function SDF_apply_with_alpha(laser_intensity = 1e4, angle = 0, target_alpha = 0.716, cat_state = false, initial_state = nothing, fock_state_n = 0, n_th_set = 10000.0, gamma_0_set = 1e-2)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Common Trap Initialization
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    trap_freq = 19e5 
    ion = Ca40([("S1/2", -1/2, "g"), ("D5/2", -5/2, "e")])
    chain = LinearChain(ions=[ion], comfrequencies=(x=3e6, y=3e6, z=trap_freq), selectedmodes=(; z=[1]))

    mode_z = zmodes(chain)[1] 
    mode_z.N = 50
    mode_z.shape = [51]

    k_vec = (x̂ + ẑ) / √2
    ϵ_vec = ŷ
    B_field = 1e-13
    
    trap_pre = Chamber(iontrap=chain, B=B_field, Bhat=ẑ)
    transition_λ = transitionwavelength(ion, ("g", "e"), trap_pre)
    mode = zmodes(trap_pre)[1]

    ψ_ion = normalize(ion["g"])
    ψ_mode = fockstate(mode, fock_state_n)
    
    ψ_initial = initial_state !== nothing ? initial_state : (ψ_ion ⊗ ψ_mode)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Physics Calculation
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    hbar = 1.0545718e-34       
    amu = 1.66053906e-27       
    m_Ca40 = 39.96259 * amu    
    
    omega_trap = 2 * π * trap_freq
    z_zpf = sqrt(hbar / (2 * m_Ca40 * omega_trap))
    k_total = 2 * π / transition_λ
    k_z = k_total / sqrt(2)
    eta = k_z * z_zpf

    dummy_laser = Laser(I=laser_intensity, k=k_vec, ϵ=ϵ_vec, λ=transition_λ)
    Bhat_tuple = (; x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0)
    
    Omega_eff_Hz = IonSim.matrixelement(ion, ("g", "e"), laser_intensity, polarization(dummy_laser), wavevector(dummy_laser), Bhat_tuple)
    Omega_eff = Omega_eff_Hz * 2 * π

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. SEQUENCE EXECUTION
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    if cat_state
        # =========================================================
        # PERFECT OPERATOR MATH: Alpha Readout (No readout noise)
        # =========================================================
        alpha_complex = target_alpha * exp(1im * angle)
        g = ion["g"]
        e = ion["e"]
        
        x_plus = normalize(g + e)
        x_minus = normalize(g - e)
        
        P_plus = x_plus ⊗ dagger(x_plus)
        P_minus = x_minus ⊗ dagger(x_minus)
        
        D_plus = IonSim.displace(mode, alpha_complex)
        D_minus = IonSim.displace(mode, -alpha_complex)
        
        U_SDF = (P_plus ⊗ D_plus) + (P_minus ⊗ D_minus)
        
        if isa(ψ_initial, Operator)
            return U_SDF * ψ_initial * dagger(U_SDF)
        else
            return U_SDF * ψ_initial
        end
        
    else
        # =========================================================
        # CONTINUOUS LINDBLAD DISPLACEMENT: Beta Signal (With Noise)
        # =========================================================
        I_spin = identityoperator(ion["g"].basis)  
        n_th = n_th_set           
        gamma_0 = gamma_0_set  
    
        gamma_plus_us = (gamma_0 * n_th) * 1e-6 
        gamma_minus_us = (gamma_0 * (n_th + 1)) * 1e-6 

        temp_fock_basis = FockBasis(mode.N) 
        a_op = DenseOperator(mode, mode, QuantumOptics.destroy(temp_fock_basis).data)
        at_op = DenseOperator(mode, mode, QuantumOptics.create(temp_fock_basis).data)

        # CRITICAL FIX: Lock the simulation time to the beta=1.0 baseline.
        # This guarantees identical ODE grid steps for finite difference.
        baseline_beta = 1.0 
        target_time_s = (2 * baseline_beta) / (eta * Omega_eff)
        target_time_us = target_time_s * 1e6

        # The target_alpha (beta + d_beta) now scales the Hamiltonian amplitude!
        H_m = (1im * target_alpha / target_time_us) * (exp(1im * angle) * at_op - exp(-1im * angle) * a_op)
        H_sys = I_spin ⊗ H_m

        a_sys = I_spin ⊗ a_op
        at_sys = I_spin ⊗ at_op

        J_cool = sqrt(gamma_minus_us) * a_sys
        J_heat = sqrt(gamma_plus_us) * at_sys
        J_ops = [J_cool, J_heat]
        J_ops_dag = dagger.(J_ops)

        function f_dyn(time_t, rho_state)
            return (H_sys, J_ops, J_ops_dag)
        end

        rho_initial = isa(ψ_initial, Ket) ? dm(ψ_initial) : ψ_initial
        
        # We only need the start and end points for the solver now
        tspan_sdf = [0.0, target_time_us]

        println("Simulating pure continuous Beta displacement with Lindblad noise...")
        # Added strict tolerances to completely eliminate numerical ODE phase drift
        _, sol_beta = timeevolution.master_dynamic(tspan_sdf, rho_initial, f_dyn, reltol=1e-10, abstol=1e-12)

        return sol_beta[end]
    end
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# TRAP SETUP[cite: 3]
# ---------------------------------------------------------
trap_freq = 19e5 
ion = Ca40([("S1/2", -1/2, "g"), ("D5/2", -5/2, "e")])
chain = LinearChain(ions=[ion], comfrequencies=(x=3e6, y=3e6, z=trap_freq), selectedmodes=(; z=[1]))
trap_pre = Chamber(iontrap=chain, B=1e-13, Bhat=ẑ)
sim_mode = zmodes(trap_pre)[1]
sim_mode.N = 50
sim_mode.shape = [51]

ion_g = normalize(ion["g"])
b_fock = FockBasis(50)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# GENERATE AND EXPORT STEP-BY-STEP IMAGES
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# STEP 1: Ground Fock State
state_0_m = Ket(sim_mode, fockstate(b_fock, 0).data)
state_1 = ion_g ⊗ state_0_m
plot_wigner_export(state_1, "1. Ground Fock State |0>", "step1_ground_fock.png")

# STEP 2: Higher Fock State |3>
state_3_m = Ket(sim_mode, fockstate(b_fock, 3).data)
state_2 = ion_g ⊗ state_3_m
plot_wigner_export(state_2, "2. Higher Fock State |3>", "step2_higher_fock.png")

# STEP 3: High Fock with Squeezing S(r=1.0)|3>
sq_op = squeeze(b_fock, 1.0 * exp(1im * 0.0))
state_sq_3_m = Ket(sim_mode, (sq_op * fockstate(b_fock, 3)).data)
state_3 = ion_g ⊗ state_sq_3_m
plot_wigner_export(state_3, "3. Squeezed Fock State S(r=1.0)|3>", "step3_squeezed_fock.png")

# STEP 4: Applied Beta Image (Signal Injection)[cite: 3]
# Uses continuous Lindblad displacement (cat_state = false)
state_4 = SDF_apply_with_alpha(1e4, 0.0, 1.0, false, state_3, 3, 0.0, 1e-2)
plot_wigner_export(state_4, "4. Displaced State (β Signal Applied)", "step4_beta_signal.png")

# STEP 5: Applied Alpha Image (Spin-Dependent Force Readout)[cite: 3]
# Applies perfect operator math for readout (cat_state = true)
state_5 = SDF_apply_with_alpha(1e4, pi/2, 0.7, true, state_4, 3, 0.0, 1e-2)
plot_wigner_export(state_5, "5. Entangled State (α Readout SDF Applied)", "step5_alpha_sdf.png")

# STEP 6: Partial Traced and Collapsed Spin Density Matrix
plot_spin_density(state_5, "6. Spin Density Matrix (Motional Modes Traced Out)", "step6_spin_density.png")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# CORRECTED EXPORT HELPERS FOR PPT
# ---------------------------------------------------------
function plot_wigner_export(final_state, title_str, filename; project_spin=false, ion=nothing)
    if project_spin
        # To see the true cat state fringes, project spin onto |+> 
        spin_plus = normalize(ion["g"] + ion["e"])
        proj_plus = dm(spin_plus)
        I_mot = identityoperator(FockBasis(50))
        
        projected_state = (proj_plus ⊗ I_mot) * final_state * (proj_plus ⊗ I_mot)
        rho_motional = ptrace(projected_state, 1)
        
        # Normalize the state after projection
        rho_motional = rho_motional / tr(rho_motional)
    else
        # Just trace out spin for standard unentangled states
        rho_motional = ptrace(final_state, 1) 
    end
    
    b_fock = FockBasis(50)
    rho_fock = DenseOperator(b_fock, rho_motional.data)

    x_vec = -4.0:0.1:4.0
    p_vec = -4.0:0.1:4.0
    W = wigner(rho_fock, x_vec, p_vec)

    fig = figure(figsize=(7, 5.5))
    subplots_adjust(bottom=0.15, left=0.15, top=0.9, right=0.95)

    PyPlot.pcolormesh(x_vec, p_vec, W, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-0.1, vmax=0.3, shading="nearest")
    cbar = PyPlot.colorbar()
    cbar.set_label("Wigner Function W(x, p)", labelpad=15)

    PyPlot.plot([0], [0], "w+", markersize=15, markeredgewidth=2, label="Original Vacuum |0>")
    
    PyPlot.xlabel("Position (x)", fontsize=12)
    PyPlot.ylabel("Momentum (p)", fontsize=12)
    PyPlot.title(title_str, fontsize=14, pad=15)
    PyPlot.grid(color="white", alpha=0.2)
    
    savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    display(fig)
end

function plot_spin_density(state, title_str, filename)
    rho_spin = ptrace(state, 2)
    fig, ax = PyPlot.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    
    Z = abs.(rho_spin.data)
    cax = ax.matshow(Z, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1)
    fig.colorbar(cax, label="Absolute Value |ρ|")
    
    for (i, j) in Iterators.product(1:2, 1:2)
        val = round(Z[i, j], digits=3)
        ax.text(j-1, i-1, string(val), ha="center", va="center", color="black", fontsize=14)
    end
    
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1])
    ax.set_xticklabels(["|g⟩", "|e⟩"], fontsize=14)
    ax.set_yticks([0, 1])
    ax.set_yticklabels(["⟨g|", "⟨e|"], fontsize=14)
    
    PyPlot.title(title_str, fontsize=14, pad=20)
    savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    display(fig)
end

function SDF_apply_with_alpha(laser_intensity = 1e4, angle = 0, target_alpha = 0.716, cat_state = false, initial_state = nothing, fock_state_n = 0, n_th_set = 10000.0, gamma_0_set = 1e-2)

    trap_freq = 19e5 
    ion = Ca40([("S1/2", -1/2, "g"), ("D5/2", -5/2, "e")])
    chain = LinearChain(ions=[ion], comfrequencies=(x=3e6, y=3e6, z=trap_freq), selectedmodes=(; z=[1]))
    trap_pre = Chamber(iontrap=chain, B=1e-13, Bhat=ẑ)
    transition_λ = transitionwavelength(ion, ("g", "e"), trap_pre)
    
    mode = zmodes(trap_pre)[1]
    # FIX: Explicitly update both the cutoff N and the underlying shape array
    mode.N = 50
    mode.shape = [51]

    ψ_ion = normalize(ion["g"])
    ψ_mode = fockstate(mode, fock_state_n)
    ψ_initial = initial_state !== nothing ? initial_state : (ψ_ion ⊗ ψ_mode)

    if cat_state
        alpha_complex = target_alpha * exp(1im * angle)
        g, e = ion["g"], ion["e"]
        x_plus, x_minus = normalize(g + e), normalize(g - e)
        
        P_plus = x_plus ⊗ dagger(x_plus)
        P_minus = x_minus ⊗ dagger(x_minus)
        D_plus = IonSim.displace(mode, alpha_complex)
        D_minus = IonSim.displace(mode, -alpha_complex)
        
        U_SDF = (P_plus ⊗ D_plus) + (P_minus ⊗ D_minus)
        
        return isa(ψ_initial, Operator) ? (U_SDF * ψ_initial * dagger(U_SDF)) : (U_SDF * ψ_initial)
        
    else
        I_spin = identityoperator(ion["g"].basis)  
        gamma_plus_us = (gamma_0_set * n_th_set) * 1e-6 
        gamma_minus_us = (gamma_0_set * (n_th_set + 1.0)) * 1e-6 

        temp_fock_basis = FockBasis(mode.N) 
        a_op = DenseOperator(mode, mode, QuantumOptics.destroy(temp_fock_basis).data)
        at_op = DenseOperator(mode, mode, QuantumOptics.create(temp_fock_basis).data)

        hbar, amu = 1.0545718e-34, 1.66053906e-27       
        omega_trap = 2 * π * trap_freq
        eta = ((2 * π / transition_λ) / sqrt(2)) * sqrt(hbar / (2 * (39.96259 * amu) * omega_trap))

        dummy_laser = Laser(I=laser_intensity, k=(x̂ + ẑ)/√2, ϵ=ŷ, λ=transition_λ)
        Omega_eff = IonSim.matrixelement(ion, ("g", "e"), laser_intensity, polarization(dummy_laser), wavevector(dummy_laser), (; x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0)) * 2 * π

        target_time_us = ((2 * 1.0) / (eta * Omega_eff)) * 1e6

        H_m = (1im * target_alpha / target_time_us) * (exp(1im * angle) * at_op - exp(-1im * angle) * a_op)
        H_sys = I_spin ⊗ H_m

        J_ops = [sqrt(gamma_minus_us) * (I_spin ⊗ a_op), sqrt(gamma_plus_us) * (I_spin ⊗ at_op)]
        rho_initial = isa(ψ_initial, Ket) ? dm(ψ_initial) : ψ_initial

        println("Simulating pure continuous Beta displacement with Lindblad noise...")
        _, sol_beta = timeevolution.master([0.0, target_time_us], rho_initial, H_sys, J_ops, reltol=1e-10, abstol=1e-12)

        return sol_beta[end]
    end
end

ion = Ca40([("S1/2", -1/2, "g"), ("D5/2", -5/2, "e")])

trap_pre = Chamber(iontrap=chain, B=1e-13, Bhat=ẑ)
sim_mode = zmodes(trap_pre)[1]
sim_mode.N = 50
sim_mode.shape = [51]

ion_g = normalize(ion["g"])
b_fock = FockBasis(50)

# STEP 1: Ground Fock State
state_0_m = Ket(sim_mode, fockstate(b_fock, 0).data)
state_1 = ion_g ⊗ state_0_m
plot_wigner_export(state_1, "1. Ground Fock State |0>", "step1_ground_fock.png")

# STEP 2: Higher Fock State |3>
state_3_m = Ket(sim_mode, fockstate(b_fock, 3).data)
state_2 = ion_g ⊗ state_3_m
plot_wigner_export(state_2, "2. Higher Fock State |3>", "step2_higher_fock.png")

# STEP 3: High Fock with Squeezing S(r=1.0)|3> (Squeezed along P, wide along X)
sq_op = squeeze(b_fock, 1.0 * exp(1im * 0.0))
state_sq_3_m = Ket(sim_mode, (sq_op * fockstate(b_fock, 3)).data)

plot_wigner_export(state_3, "3. Squeezed Fock State S(r=1.0)|3>", "step3_squeezed_fock.png")

# STEP 4: Applied Beta Image (Signal Injection)
# THEORY: Beta = ib (Imaginary -> P-axis momentum displacement)
# Fixed: We use angle = pi/2 for the beta displacement along the narrow P-axis
state_4 = SDF_apply_with_alpha(1e4, pi/2, 1.0, false, state_3, 3, 0.0, 1e-2)
plot_wigner_export(state_4, "4. Displaced State (β Signal Applied along P)", "step4_beta_signal.png")

# STEP 5: Applied Alpha Image (Spin-Dependent Force Readout)
# THEORY: Alpha = a (Real -> X-axis position displacement)
# Fixed: We use angle = 0.0 to split the state horizontally along the wide X-axis
state_5 = SDF_apply_with_alpha(1e4, 0.0, 1.5, true, state_4, 3, 0.0, 1e-2)
# Fixed: Use project_spin=true to reveal the interference fringes!
plot_wigner_export(state_5, "5. Entangled Cat State (α Readout SDF)\nProjected on Spin |+⟩", "step5_alpha_sdf.png", project_spin=true, ion=ion)

# STEP 6: Partial Traced and Collapsed Spin Density Matrix
plot_spin_density(state_5, "6. Spin Density Matrix (Motional Modes Traced Out)", "step6_spin_density.png")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# CORRECTED EXPORT HELPERS FOR PPT
# ---------------------------------------------------------
function plot_wigner_export(final_state, title_str, filename; project_spin=false, ion=nothing)
    if project_spin
        # To see the true cat state fringes, project spin onto |+> 
        spin_plus = normalize(ion["g"] + ion["e"])
        proj_plus = dm(spin_plus)
        
        # FIX: Dynamically extract the exact VibrationalMode basis to avoid IncompatibleBases
        motional_basis = final_state.basis_l.bases[2]
        I_mot = identityoperator(motional_basis)
        
        projected_state = (proj_plus ⊗ I_mot) * final_state * (proj_plus ⊗ I_mot)
        rho_motional = ptrace(projected_state, 1)
        
        # Normalize the state after projection
        rho_motional = rho_motional / tr(rho_motional)
    else
        # Just trace out spin for standard unentangled states
        rho_motional = ptrace(final_state, 1) 
    end
    
    # Coerce back into a standard QuantumOptics FockBasis to use the wigner() function
    b_fock = FockBasis(50)
    rho_fock = DenseOperator(b_fock, rho_motional.data)

    x_vec = -8.0:0.1:8.0
    p_vec = -8.0:0.1:8.0
    W = wigner(rho_fock, x_vec, p_vec)

    fig = figure(figsize=(7, 5.5))
    subplots_adjust(bottom=0.15, left=0.15, top=0.9, right=0.95)

    PyPlot.pcolormesh(x_vec, p_vec, W, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-0.1, vmax=0.3, shading="nearest")
    cbar = PyPlot.colorbar()
    cbar.set_label("Wigner Function W(x, p)", labelpad=15)

    PyPlot.plot([0], [0], "w+", markersize=15, markeredgewidth=2, label="Original Vacuum |0>")
    
    PyPlot.xlabel("Position (x)", fontsize=12)
    PyPlot.ylabel("Momentum (p)", fontsize=12)
    PyPlot.title(title_str, fontsize=14, pad=15)
    PyPlot.grid(color="white", alpha=0.2)
    
    savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    display(fig)
end

# STEP 3: High Fock with Squeezing S(r=1.0)|3> (Squeezed along P, wide along X)

state_sq_3_m = Ket(sim_mode, (sq_op * fockstate(b_fock, 3)).data)
state_3 = ion_g ⊗ state_sq_3_m
plot_wigner_export(state_3, "3. Squeezed Fock State S(r=1.0)|3>", "step3_squeezed_fock.png")

# STEP 4: Applied Beta Image (Signal Injection)
# THEORY: Beta = ib (Imaginary -> P-axis momentum displacement)
# Fixed: We use angle = pi/2 for the beta displacement along the narrow P-axis
state_4 = SDF_apply_with_alpha(1e4, pi/2, 1.0, false, state_3, 3, 0.0, 1e-2)
plot_wigner_export(state_4, "4. Displaced State (β Signal Applied along P)", "step4_beta_signal.png")

# STEP 5: Applied Alpha Image (Spin-Dependent Force Readout)
# THEORY: Alpha = a (Real -> X-axis position displacement)
# Fixed: We use angle = 0.0 to split the state horizontally along the wide X-axis
state_5 = SDF_apply_with_alpha(1e4, 0.0, 1.5, true, state_4, 3, 0.0, 1e-2)
# Fixed: Use project_spin=true to reveal the interference fringes!
plot_wigner_export(state_5, "5. Entangled Cat State (α Readout SDF)\nProjected on Spin |+⟩", "step5_alpha_sdf.png", project_spin=true, ion=ion)

# STEP 6: Partial Traced and Collapsed Spin Density Matrix
plot_spin_density(state_5, "6. Spin Density Matrix (Motional Modes Traced Out)", "step6_spin_density.png")
